chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:
"Everything in the human being of which there are two, then in both of them is the diyah, and in one of them is half of the diyah; and whatever is single, then in it is the diyah."

key_terms.أَحَدِهِمَا: one of the two paired members
key_terms.اَلدِّيَةُ: prescribed blood money or legal compensation for bodily injury
key_terms.اَلْإِنْسَانِ: the human being, whose bodily members are under discussion
key_terms.اِثْنَانِ: two, referring to paired limbs or organs
key_terms.نِصْفُ: half, indicating half of the diyah for one of a pair
key_terms.وَاحِدًا: single, referring to an unpaired organ or member

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on diyah for paired and single human organs in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal principle for bodily injury compensation in Islamic law. For paired organs or limbs, the full diyah applies to both together and half applies to one; for a single organ, the full diyah applies.
